_note: Seed data for siya_decisions. decision_date fields are approximate (August 2026 build window) — exact dates were not tracked at the time these decisions were made in conversation. Review before treating dates as precise. owner_department defaults to 'Founder' unless a specific team owns the decision.
_authority: Postgres siya_decisions is the authoritative store. Memory hub UI is the sole create/edit path going forward. This JSON is a one-time import; markdown under decisions/*.md is boot-synced then treated as export/backup.

_overlap.homepage-cta-meet-and-greet: Related to seed id meet-greet-replaced-discovery-call (CTA vs Discovery Call retirement) — both kept, linked via relates_to
_overlap.marketing-os-v1-frozen: Related to seed id marketing-bigger-systems-paused — both kept, linked via relates_to
_overlap.agent-org-chart-deferred: No duplicate in this seed (distinct from personal-ai-coach-deferred)

decisions.title: MVP v1 scope locked before new features
decisions.decision_text: Verify and stabilize everything already built (tasks/SOPs, chat review, handoffs, nav/token consolidation) before starting anything new.
decisions.reason: Reactive building across multiple parallel threads was causing 'reported done' vs 'actually done' gaps; needed one clean, fully-verified checkpoint.
decisions.what_changed: Personal AI coach, Zoho sync, and deep visual redesign explicitly moved to later phases, not pulled forward as 'infrastructure prep'.

decisions.title: Chat review restricted to admin + clinical lead only
decisions.decision_text: Chat QA review access is limited to admin and the clinical lead; regular staff self-report their own chat/call activity via shift handoff instead.
decisions.reason: Chat review is a QA function requiring clinical judgment; self-service access for all staff conflated QA with self-reporting.

decisions.title: Meet & Greet replaced the $79 Discovery Call
decisions.decision_text: The paid Discovery Call ($10 deposit + $69) is discontinued. The free Meet & Greet is the current, sole intro-consult offering.
decisions.reason: Website and staff knowledge had drifted out of sync, creating a pricing conflict that could mislead patients.
decisions.what_changed: Stale Discovery Call content retired from staff KB and Ask retrieval, not left alongside the correct info.

decisions.title: Founder Decision Coach is admin-only
decisions.decision_text: Founder Decision Coach / Weekly Brief is visible only to admin/founder accounts, not the entire team.
decisions.reason: It surfaces founder-level strategic signals not relevant or appropriate for general staff view.

decisions.title: Flat team structure — no manager/senior hierarchy
decisions.decision_text: The team operates flat: no formal manager/senior tier, and department leads perform the same core work as everyone else, differing only in review/lead responsibilities.
decisions.reason: Founder's explicit culture stance: avoid creating internal hierarchy or condescension between staff.

decisions.title: SiyaOS near-term north star: function as an LMS
decisions.decision_text: SiyaOS's priority is tracking progress and giving assignments — using what's already built (tasks/SOP checklists, Learn/Level-Up, chat review/handoffs) rather than pursuing new AI features or bigger marketing systems.
decisions.reason: Provides a clear filter for what's in scope: does a proposed feature help track progress or give/receive an assignment?

decisions.title: Marketing SOPs must be maximally prescriptive with built-in escalation
decisions.decision_text: SOPs for the marketing team include explicit selection criteria, minimum counts, time budgets, and mandatory capture fields, with escalation itself written in as a required, time-boxed step.
decisions.reason: Real field-testing showed the team does not proactively escalate blockers or fill ambiguity with independent judgment.

decisions.title: Nothing becomes shared company knowledge without founder approval
decisions.decision_text: Content from team interactions with SiyaOS's AI tools does not become shared/company-wide knowledge or influence company direction without explicit founder approval first.
decisions.reason: Protects against unvetted ideas or AI-influenced content silently becoming institutional 'truth'.
decisions.what_changed: Fixed a real gap where Ask retrieval included pending_review (unapproved) SOPs, not just live ones.

decisions.title: LLM Gateway failures traced to one billing gate, not three bugs
decisions.decision_text: The recurring 'LLM off' issue across Ask, SOP Builder, and Learn was a single Vercel AI Gateway billing/customer-verification gate — resolved by adding a payment method, with code fixed so this failure mode can never again be misreported as 'LLM off'.
decisions.reason: Root-cause discipline prevented three separate patch attempts for what was actually one config issue.

decisions.title: Personal AI coach deferred to a later phase
decisions.decision_text: A per-team-member personalized AI coach (named, remembers individual history over time) is scoped but explicitly deferred — not part of current build phases.
decisions.reason: Represents meaningful new infrastructure (per-user memory, distillation pipeline); deliberately sequenced after core MVP stability.

decisions.title: Knowledge SOP (paste-and-review) preferred for policy-style SOPs
decisions.decision_text: Long-form policy/prose SOPs are authored via the paste-and-review Knowledge SOP workflow; the AI interview Builder is reserved for shorter checklist-style SOPs.
decisions.reason: The AI interview approach had real quality-gate issues (initially accepted gibberish input); paste-and-review sidesteps that risk for higher-stakes policy content.

decisions.title: Marketing 'bigger systems' expansion paused
decisions.decision_text: A proposal to build six new marketing 'operating systems' (Research OS, Content OS, Distribution OS, etc.) was declined for now.
decisions.reason: The proposal inflated a messy, still-unclear team process into invented infrastructure before the team had basic process clarity; direct scope creep against the MVP lock.

decisions.title: Visual/design system locked before further feature work
decisions.decision_text: A basic, reusable design + animation system (Visual OS: cream/plum/navy palette) is being finished and locked before finalizing further features/workflows.
decisions.reason: Prevents visual inconsistency from compounding as more features ship; treats design tokens as foundational infrastructure.

decisions.title: Chat-first home screen and native team chat deferred
decisions.decision_text: A fully chat-first My Day and native team-to-team chat are not being built. Team continues using Zoho Cliq/WhatsApp for chat.
decisions.reason: Patient-related communication must stay in HIPAA-compliant tools; any future casual chat in SiyaOS would need to be strictly non-clinical.

decisions.title: Hold off on active fundraising; declined OpenVC Premium
decisions.decision_text: Not actively raising. Strengthening CAC/LTV numbers first. Declined OpenVC Premium subscription given the fundability tool's own guidance to bootstrap more or pursue an accelerator.
decisions.reason: OpenVC fundability score improved only modestly (26.77 → 31.85/100) despite corrected framing and revenue growth; tool's own guidance reinforced patience over premium outreach tools.

decisions.title: Corporate/CPOM/tax compliance requires professional counsel, not AI research
decisions.decision_text: Corporate practice of medicine (CPOM) and multi-state tax compliance questions are directed to a qualified healthcare regulatory attorney and CPA, not AI-generated research treated as authoritative.
decisions.reason: California and Texas (Siya's PC states) are high-enforcement CPOM jurisdictions with active 2026 regulatory changes; the stakes (unenforceable agreements, regulatory penalties) are too high for AI-synthesized guidance.

decisions.title: Founder Coach domain expansion phased
decisions.decision_text: Phase 1: domain tabs (Accounts, HR, Clinical, Marketing, Compliance) sourced only from real existing data, no invented content. Phase 2: lockable AI-assisted weekly plan. Phase 3 (parked): persona role-play and external data pulls.
decisions.reason: Prevents overbuilding speculative AI features before real data pipelines (like weekly lead check-ins) are proven.

decisions.title: Hybrid founder-coaching model: chat as scratchpad, OS as record
decisions.decision_text: Claude (chat) is used as a thinking-partner/sounding-board for founder decisions, but any real conclusion must be written back into SiyaOS (Founder Coach's Focus/Can Wait/Delegate/Observe fields) as the actual record.
decisions.reason: Prevents the founder's own strategic thinking from becoming the one thing NOT captured in the 'single source of truth' system, after enforcing that discipline everywhere else.

decisions.title: Data room kept external, not built into SiyaOS
decisions.decision_text: Investor data-room material (cap table, financials, legal docs) stays in a simple access-controlled external folder (Drive/Notion), not built as a SiyaOS feature.
decisions.reason: SiyaOS's current access model is staff-oriented, not designed for investor-only confidential material; premature given the company isn't actively raising.

decisions.title: Declined Google Ads Performance Max recommendation
decisions.decision_text: Not adopting Google's recommended Performance Max campaign type despite the platform's own suggestion.
decisions.reason: Still building a clean Search-only conversion baseline; PMax would mix in Display/YouTube/Discover traffic and muddy the exact signal being isolated. Google's aggregate uplift stats are not specific evidence for this campaign's stage.

decisions.title: Content/distribution tracking stays in sheets until proven manually
decisions.decision_text: Distribution and content tracking remain in spreadsheets until the distribution SOP has run manually at least once; a SiyaOS dashboard will extend the existing task/Kanban system when built, not a new one.
decisions.reason: Consistent with the build's 'prove manually, then build' pattern used for research and content QA SOPs.

decisions.title: No Google Ads/GA4 dashboard until tracking accuracy is fixed
decisions.decision_text: Will not build a SiyaOS dashboard surfacing Google Ads/GA4 metrics until known tracking issues (100% bounce rate contradiction, missing attribution) are resolved.
decisions.reason: A polished dashboard on top of known-unreliable data would make bad numbers look more trustworthy than they are.

decisions.title: Longer-term sequencing: prove the practice before raising for a tech platform
decisions.decision_text: Focus on building the ADHD practice itself using existing marketplaces (Zocdoc, Klarity) plus owned-channel ads for patient acquisition. Raise specifically to build an owned tech platform only once acquisition is proven with clean, real CAC numbers.
decisions.reason: Clinical infrastructure is already largely in place; patient acquisition is the actual open question, and real numbers are a stronger fundraising foundation than a platform pitch.

decisions.title: No-show fee $50 for direct bookings; late-cancel amount not locked
decisions.decision_text: Direct siya.health bookings: no-show fee is $50. Late-cancellation dollar amount is not locked yet — escalate to Billing rather than guessing. Klarity has separate cancel/no-show rules and must never be mixed with direct-booking rules.
decisions.reason: Staff were inventing or conflating marketplace vs owned-booking policies; only the locked $50 no-show figure is safe to quote for direct bookings.

decisions.title: No fixed practice-wide hours — weekly EHR availability only
decisions.decision_text: There is no published practice-wide schedule. Provider availability is set weekly in the EHR. Ask must say that plainly and never invent a schedule or clinic hours.
decisions.reason: Invented hours create false patient expectations; weekly EHR settings are the only real source.

decisions.title: SOP Builder and Knowledge SOP stay two separate systems
decisions.decision_text: SOP Builder (AI interview, checklist-style) and Knowledge SOP (paste-and-review, prose/policy-style) are deliberately two systems. Do not merge them.
decisions.reason: Different authoring risks and quality gates; merging would reintroduce gibberish acceptance on high-stakes policy content.

decisions.title: Chat review and shift handoff stay deliberately separate
decisions.decision_text: Chat review is QA oversight (admin/clinical lead only). Shift handoff is self-report for all staff. Different purposes — keep them separate.
decisions.reason: Conflating QA with self-reporting either weakens clinical oversight or overloads every staff member with a QA tool.

decisions.title: Pricing and provider-state facts use deterministic lookup
decisions.decision_text: Pricing and provider-state facts use deterministic exact-match lookup, not SOP semantic retrieval. Factual questions need reliability over flexible matching.
decisions.reason: Semantic retrieval can miss or blur exact dollar amounts and licensed states; exact-match facts-lookup is the safer path.

decisions.title: Siya Guide stays separate from staff Ask
decisions.decision_text: Siya Guide (patient-facing chatbot) intentionally stays a separate system from staff Ask and does not share infrastructure.
decisions.reason: Different audiences, knowledge governance, and PHI risk; merging would blur External bot vs Internal bot boundaries.

decisions.title: Prescription generator: one clinic profile near-term; multi-clinic deferred
decisions.decision_text: Near-term prescription generator scope is one clinic profile per logged-in staff user. True multi-clinic support is explicitly deferred.
decisions.reason: Multi-clinic adds identity, permissions, and template complexity before the single-clinic path is proven.

decisions.title: Mic/dictate uses free browser Web Speech API
decisions.decision_text: Mic/dictate uses the free browser-native Web Speech API instead of paid server-side transcription, specifically to avoid ongoing per-use cost.
decisions.reason: Paid transcription would add recurring cost for a convenience feature; browser-native is good enough for draft capture.

decisions.title: Resend email for SOP review and task assignment
decisions.decision_text: Resend notifications cover SOP submit/approve/send-back and task assignment/reassign emails to the assignee. Overdue reminders, billing escalation, and a founder digest remain deferred.
decisions.reason: Task assign was deferred until one Resend path was proven; SOP review mail is stable, so assignment mail reuses that BFF + RESEND_API_KEY pattern.

decisions.title: SOP quality gate judges substance via LLM, not junk-string blocklist alone
decisions.decision_text: The SOP quality gate judges substance with an LLM check, not only pattern-matching known junk strings. A keyword blocklist alone kept missing novel gibberish.
decisions.reason: Field testing showed junk inputs that passed simple string filters; substance checking catches novel nonsense.

decisions.title: Fun Friday kept as lightweight external doc, not built into SiyaOS
decisions.decision_text: Fun Friday (team culture program) was reviewed for SiyaOS integration and deliberately kept as a lightweight external doc, not built into the OS.
decisions.reason: Culture programming does not need portal modules; building it in would be scope against the LMS/MVP filter.

decisions.title: CPOM/MSO attorney docs: extraction-only, admin/compliance visibility
decisions.decision_text: Attorney-drafted CPOM/MSO corporate documents are handled extraction-only (deadlines/facts pulled out, no AI legal interpretation), restricted to admin/compliance-owner visibility, and never staff-searchable.
decisions.reason: AI legal interpretation of corporate docs is high-risk; staff Ask must not surface or opine on them.
